title: Dreamina MCP: Setup Guide and Credit Costs (2026)
summary: Dreamina MCP is a Model Context Protocol server for AI-driven image and video generation. Understand why the system failed despite its technical design.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces for Capped, Approved Generation Runs


For a repeat generation job,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , an MIT-licensed automation platform, lets you write the sequence once as a flow, and a run costs 1 credit however many steps it has, with unlimited flows on every plan, including free.


The night above was an agent with a key and nothing else: no role, no log, only code that kept running.


Activepieces puts an agent inside the same access model as your staff: RBAC, SSO and SCIM decide which connections it may use, and the enterprise RBAC docs state that those access policies apply to what an agent may connect to.


In the run detail view, every tool call an agent step makes is listed on its own line with its input and output, which is the call log the table above said was missing.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production, on an MIT-licensed core with 750 integrations, so a failure here affects these four companies and 750 integration points. None of this replaces a Dreamina MCP server; it governs what runs around one.


### A fixed sequence instead of an improvising agent


Where an agent improvises, a workflow doesn't. You write the sequence once: take the brief, build the prompt, request the generation, check the result, deliver it.


Each step is a node, so the agent can't add a sixth step or loop back to the third on a whim.


Put the retry limit on the step, not in a sentence in a prompt the model may ignore. A failed generation stops after the limit and reports, instead of resubmitting forever.


The approval step puts a pause before the expensive node, so nothing's requested until a person says yes.


### Exposing the workflow over MCP


Here's where MCP comes in: Activepieces can expose a flow as a tool to MCP-capable clients such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor, and MCPs are included on the free plan, which comes with 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows.


The assistant then doesn't see "generate anything, any time."


It sees one bounded tool, such as "run the approved product-shot job," and whatever sits behind it's the workflow's steps, limits and pause.


The comparison below shows the difference in where the loop lives, and the point to take from it's that the cap sits in the workflow, outside the model's reach.


### What this doesn't change


Do not expect any of this to change Dreamina's pricing. Each generation still costs what Dreamina charges, and a workflow only controls how many you can trigger and who signs off.


Search the 750 integrations in Activepieces' open source monorepo, under packages/integrations/community, for a Dreamina connector before you plan around one, in case it already exists.


If there isn't one, the generation step has to go through a generic HTTP request, which is more setup for you.
